extracted.intended_audience: aspiring and practicing romance writers (members/readers of Romance Writers of America)
extracted.subtask_description: Genre-level guidance describing what qualifies as a romance novel and how to classify and craft works within romance subgenres. Useful for writers aiming to produce commercially and generically recognizable romance fiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Central Love Story
rubrics_metrics.description: The main plot centers around individuals falling in love and struggling to make the relationship work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A writer can include as many subplots as they want as long as the love story is the main focus of the novel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotionally Satisfying and Optimistic Ending
rubrics_metrics.description: An emotionally satisfying and optimistic ending: in a romance, the lovers who risk and struggle for each other and their relationship are rewarded with emotional justice and unconditional love.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ending should provide emotional closure and an optimistic resolution for the central relationship; this is a defining element of the genre.

rubrics_metrics.name: Love Story Must Remain the Primary Focus
rubrics_metrics.description: The writer may include subplots, but the love story must remain the main focus of the novel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subplots are acceptable so long as they do not eclipse the central romantic plot; genre classification depends on this focal priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone, Style, Setting, and Sensuality Are Flexible
rubrics_metrics.description: Romance novels may have any tone or style, be set in any place or time, and have varying levels of sensuality—ranging from sweet to extremely hot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These variations create specific subgenres within romance fiction; authors may choose tone/style/sensuality appropriate to their subgenre while maintaining the central love story and satisfying ending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contemporary Romance (subgenre criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Contemporary Romance: Romance novels that are set from 1950 to the present that focus primarily on the romantic relationship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Setting (post-1950) and emphasis on the romantic relationship are the classification markers for contemporary romance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Erotic Romance (subgenre criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Erotic Romance: Romance novels in which strong, often explicit, sexual interaction is an inherent part of the love story, character growth and relationship development and could not be removed without damaging the storyline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These novels may contain elements of other romance subgenres (such as paranormal, historical, etc.). The sexual content is integral to plot and character development rather than merely titillating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical Romance (subgenre criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Historical Romance: Romance novels that are set prior to 1950.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time-period setting (pre-1950) is the defining characteristic; historical context should be integral to plot, character, or atmosphere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paranormal Romance (subgenre criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Paranormal Romance: Romance novels in which fantasy worlds or paranormal or science fiction elements are an integral part of the plot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supernatural, fantastical, or sci‑fi elements must be central to the story rather than incidental.

rubrics_metrics.name: Romance with Spiritual Elements (subgenre criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Romance with Spiritual Elements: Romance novels in which spiritual beliefs are an inherent part of the love story, character growth or relationship development, and could not be removed without damaging the storyline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These novels may be set in the context of any religious or spiritual belief system or culture; spiritual elements must be integral to the romance and character arcs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Romantic Suspense (subgenre criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Romantic Suspense: Romance novels in which suspense, mystery, or thriller elements constitute an integral part of the plot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspense/mystery/thriller components should be essential to the story and entwined with the romantic plot rather than separate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Young Adult Romance (subgenre criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Young Adult Romance: Romance novels in which young adult life is an integral part of the plot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: YA life stage, concerns, and perspective should be central to the plot and character development; often targets younger readers and may affect tone, content, and marketing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Reader Demographics and Habits to Inform Writing/Marketing
rubrics_metrics.description: Profile and reading habits: typical romance reader (2017 study) is 82% female, average age 35–39, with ethnic and sexual-orientation distributions noted; 92% are print readers, 64% e-book readers, 35% audiobook users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Younger readers skew toward YA, erotic, and paranormal romance and use digital/audiobook formats more; readers acquire books through libraries, brick-and-mortar stores, friends, and online stores. Authors should consider these demographics and acquisition/format preferences when tailoring content and marketing.
